title: Add analysis_template to AgentAdapter for non-streaming invocation mode
description:
## Problem

WeaveStrand and UnravelStrand invoke agents via CliWeaveAgent / CliUnravelAgent, which run:
  cd {workspace} && {agent_cmd} --print < {prompt_file}

agent_cmd is config.agent.default — the dispatch adapter NAME (e.g. claude-code-glm-4.7), not a PATH binary. ZAI/GLM adapters are not in PATH and require specific env vars. They also use --output-format stream-json, which weave cannot parse as plain text bead proposals.

## Fix

Add analysis_template: Option<String> to AgentAdapter in dispatch/mod.rs.
- When Some: shell command template for analysis-mode invocation. Supports {workspace} and {prompt_file}. Must use --print, must NOT use --output-format stream-json.
- When None: fall back to: cd {workspace} && {agent_cli} --print < {prompt_file}

Add AgentAdapter::analysis_command(workspace, prompt_file) -> String rendering the template.
Update all builtin adapters to set analysis_template. Validate that {prompt_file} is present when set.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AgentAdapter has analysis_template: Option<String> with full serde support
- [ ] AgentAdapter::analysis_command(workspace, prompt_file) renders with substitution
- [ ] Fallback when None: cd {workspace} && {agent_cli} --print < {prompt_file}
- [ ] Validation: analysis_template must contain {prompt_file} when set
- [ ] Builtin adapters (claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-opus, etc.) have analysis_template set
- [ ] Unit tests: rendering, None fallback, missing-{prompt_file} validation error

title: Trace Telemetry::new() vs Telemetry::from_config() fallback path
description:
## Investigation: Does Telemetry::new() create a FileSink?

`src/cli/mod.rs:637-641` shows the telemetry init path:

```rust
let telemetry =
    Telemetry::from_config(qualified_id.clone(), &config.telemetry).unwrap_or_else(|e| {
        tracing::warn!(error = %e, "failed to create hook-enabled telemetry, falling back");
        Telemetry::new(qualified_id.clone())
    });
```

If `from_config()` fails, it falls back to `Telemetry::new()`. Need to check:

1. Does `Telemetry::new()` include a FileSink, or is it a no-op/null emitter?
2. What does `from_config()` require that might be missing?
3. Is `config.telemetry.file_sink.enabled` set to true?

### Files to investigate
- `src/telemetry/mod.rs` — Telemetry::new() and Telemetry::from_config() constructors
- `src/config/mod.rs` — default telemetry config values

Depends on: needle-la6l

title: Mend Strand: Earlier Cleanup for Zero-Activity Worker Logs
description:
## Mend Strand: Earlier Cleanup for Zero-Activity Worker Logs

### Problem
Agent log files from workers that crash immediately (0 beads processed) persist for `retention_days` before being cleaned up. These logs are typically short and contain only startup/error information, so there's no value in keeping them for the full retention period.

### Root Cause
- `cleanup_old_agent_logs()$ only checks file age
- No correlation between log files and worker registry entries
- Workers with `beads_processed == 0` leave logs that linger unnecessarily

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Mend strand detects agent logs from workers with 0 beads processed
- [ ] Logs from zero-activity workers are cleaned up immediately (not retained)
- [ ] Telemetry event emitted for each early-cleaned log
- [ ] Test coverage for zero-activity log detection
- [ ] Integration test verifies zero-activity logs are removed

### Implementation Notes
- Modify `cleanup_old_agent_logs()` or add new step
- Parse worker ID from log filename (format: `{worker}-{bead}.agent.jsonl`)
- Check registry for worker entry and `beads_processed` count
- If `beads_processed == 0`, delete log immediately
- Emit `EventKind::MendZeroActivityLogCleaned` (may need new event kind)
- Edge case: log file for worker no longer in registry → treat as zero-activity

### Dependencies
- None

### Related
- Bead: needle-9hu7 (this audit)
- File: src/strand/mend.rs
- Config: log_dir, retention_days
close_reason: Implementation already complete in prior session. The zero-activity worker log cleanup feature is fully implemented: 1) Detection via cleanup_old_agent_logs, 2) Immediate cleanup regardless of age, 3) Telemetry event emitted, 4) Edge cases handled, 5) Integration test verifies behavior. Test: PASSED

title: Epic: CLAUDE.md Placement Strategy for Promoted Learnings
description:
## Epic: CLAUDE.md Placement Strategy for Promoted Learnings

### Context
When reflect promotes a high-frequency learning, it should write it into the CLAUDE.md file at the lowest common ancestor directory covering all workspaces where the pattern was observed. This ensures the learning appears in the system prompt only when working in relevant projects.

### Requirements
- Track which workspaces contributed each pattern during extraction
- Find the deepest CLAUDE.md whose directory is a parent of all contributing workspaces
- If no CLAUDE.md exists at that level, create one with appropriate frontmatter
- Append the learning under a `## NEEDLE Learnings` section
- Avoid duplicating learnings already present in the file
- Handle edge case: pattern observed in only one workspace → write to that workspace's CLAUDE.md
- Handle edge case: pattern observed across all workspaces → write to ~/CLAUDE.md

title: Fix: orphaned cargo test processes spin at 300%+ CPU

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
## Bug: Orphaned cargo test processes burn CPU indefinitely

### Problem
When needle workers are dispatched beads in the NEEDLE workspace, they run cargo test --lib
(forbidden by NEEDLE CLAUDE.md). The test binary gets stuck in a tokio busy loop. When the
worker is killed, the test process is orphaned (PPID -> 1) and spins at 300%+ CPU indefinitely.

### Observed symptoms
- 4 orphaned needle-187fa8a8441893d8 processes each consuming 300%+ CPU
- Running 5+ hours with no exit, total impact ~1000% CPU (10+ cores pegged)
- System load 28-44, swap 16GB/32GB

### Root cause
1. Worker runs cargo test --lib -- --test-threads=1 in NEEDLE repo
2. 323 tokio::test functions compiled into one binary
3. One or more tests create tokio runtimes with infinite loops (no timeout)
4. Worker killed -> cargo dies -> test binary orphaned -> spins forever

### Fix needed
Part 1: Global test timeout - enforce per-test timeouts via test harness or Cargo.toml
Part 2: Worker guard - respect CLAUDE.md, dont run cargo test in NEEDLE repo

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All NEEDLE tests have explicit timeouts
- [ ] default-test-timeout in Cargo.toml or test harness
- [ ] Orphaned test processes eventually exit

title: Fix WeaveStrand and UnravelStrand to apply error backoff when agent invocation fails
description:
## Problem

In WeaveStrand::evaluate (weave.rs ~line 409), when the agent invocation fails (analyze_gaps returns Err), the strand returns StrandResult::Error immediately WITHOUT updating state.last_run. Since last_run is never updated on error, the cooldown never accumulates and weave retries the failing subprocess spawn every idle cycle — typically 4-8ms of wasted work per waterfall pass with no relief.

The parse-failure path (line ~421) correctly updates last_run to prevent rapid retries, but the agent-failure path does not.

Same issue exists in UnravelStrand (unravel.rs).

## Fix

In weave.rs (agent failure branch):
  - Before returning StrandResult::Error, update state.last_run = Some(Utc::now())
  - Call state.save(&state_path) to persist
  - Use the full cooldown_hours so agent errors get the same backoff as successful runs

Same fix in unravel.rs for CliUnravelAgent failure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] weave.rs: agent invocation failure updates last_run before returning Error
- [ ] unravel.rs: same fix applied
- [ ] Unit test: agent failure → state file written with last_run set, second call returns NoWork (cooldown not elapsed)
- [ ] Confirm existing agent_failure_returns_error test still passes (still returns Error, just also saves state)

title: Workers hang forever when claude loses TCP connection to zai-proxy
description:
## Bug: Stuck workers after zai-proxy TCP connection loss

### Symptom
Workers transition to EXECUTING state and spawn claude, but claude never connects to (or immediately loses connection to) zai-proxy. Claude enters an infinite idle wait (0.4% CPU, no network sockets). The needle worker waits forever for the claude subprocess to exit.

### Trigger
High CPU load (~18) caused by concurrent debug builds caused claude processes to fail to establish TCP connections. All 5 affected workers stalled simultaneously at ~May 4 03:15 UTC.

### Affected workers (2026-05-05)
- alpha (miroir): stuck 31h, bead miroir-r3j
- delta (NEEDLE): stuck 31h, bead needle-pfan
- papa (mobile-gaming): stuck 31h, bead bf-3ci04
- bravo (HOOP): stuck 31h, bead hoop-ttb
- charlie (bead-forge): stuck 30h, bead bf-4ir

### Root cause
NEEDLE has no stuck-process detection. After dispatching claude, the worker waits for the subprocess to exit. If claude goes idle (no API calls, no output) for an extended period, the worker should kill it and retry, but there is no such watchdog.

### Evidence
- All stuck claude PIDs have 0 TCP connections (verified with ss -tnp)
- Only unix socket connections to bash parent process
- All stuck at state EXECUTING with no telemetry events after transform.skipped
- needle status shows 0 beads completed for stuck workers

### Fix needed
Add a stuck-process watchdog to the agent execution loop:
1. After dispatching claude, monitor for API activity (telemetry events or stdout output)
2. If no activity for N minutes (configurable, suggest 10-15min), send SIGTERM to claude process
3. After SIGTERM grace period, SIGKILL
4. Release the bead as deferred and retry
5. Log the stuck-detection event for observability

title: feat: randomize idle backoff between configurable min/max bounds
description:
## Problem

When multiple workers enter EXHAUSTED state (e.g., after consecutive claim race losses), they all back off for the same fixed idle_timeout duration (currently 900s). When they wake simultaneously, they thundering-herd back into claim contention, and many lose races again — repeating the cycle.

## Approach

Replace the fixed idle_timeout backoff with a random duration sampled from [idle_timeout_min, idle_timeout_max]:

- Add idle_timeout_min and idle_timeout_max fields to WorkerConfig (defaults: 60, 120)
- Deprecate the existing idle_timeout field (log a warning if still set, use it as idle_timeout_max if idle_timeout_min/idle_timeout_max are absent — backward compat)
- In handle_exhausted, use rand::Rng::gen_range(idle_timeout_min..=idle_timeout_max) instead of the fixed value
- Add rand to Cargo.toml if not already a dependency (check first)
- Log the sampled backoff value: backoff_secs=<sampled> range=[min,max]

## Config precedence

idle_timeout_min + idle_timeout_max → used directly
idle_timeout alone → min=60, max=idle_timeout (backward compat)
neither → min=60, max=120

## Acceptance

- [ ] Workers in EXHAUSTED state back off for a random duration between configurable bounds
- [ ] Existing idle_timeout config still works (backward compat)
- [ ] Log line shows the sampled value and range
- [ ] cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings passes
- [ ] cargo fmt passes

title: Thread adapter analysis_template into WeaveStrand and UnravelStrand
description:
## Problem

StrandRunner::from_config constructs CliWeaveAgent and CliUnravelAgent with config.agent.default (the adapter name as if it were a binary). It never resolves the adapter config, so the ZAI proxy env vars, correct model flags, and analysis_template are all ignored.

## Fix (depends on bf-1307a)

In StrandRunner::from_config:
1. Accept the adapter registry (or the resolved Dispatcher) so adapter configs are accessible.
2. Look up the adapter by config.agent.default.
3. Call adapter.analysis_command(workspace, prompt_file) to get the full shell command.
4. Pass that command string to CliWeaveAgent::new and CliUnravelAgent::new.
5. If the adapter is not found, fall back to the current behavior (agent_cmd binary + --print).

CliWeaveAgent and CliUnravelAgent already write the prompt to a tmp file and shell out; they just need to use the resolved command instead of constructing their own.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] StrandRunner::from_config resolves the adapter by name from the dispatcher/adapter registry
- [ ] CliWeaveAgent receives the full analysis_command string, not just a binary name
- [ ] CliUnravelAgent same
- [ ] GLM workers: weave and unravel run with ZAI proxy env vars correctly set
- [ ] Fallback: adapter not found -> {agent_cmd} --print < {prompt_file} (current behavior preserved)
- [ ] Integration test: mock adapter with analysis_template -> weave invokes the full command
- [ ] worker.rs caller of StrandRunner::from_config updated to pass adapter registry

title: Weave strand only analyzes default workspace, ignores explore workspaces
description:
WeaveStrand is constructed with config.workspace.default (/home/coding/NEEDLE) in StrandRunner::from_config (src/strand/mod.rs:157-163). It never analyzes explore workspaces. When workers exhaust beads from an explore workspace (e.g. vibe-coding-discovery), weave fires but analyzes NEEDLE docs instead of that workspace's plan.md.

Two sub-problems:
1. Workspace: WeaveStrand.workspace is always config.workspace.default — explore workspaces are never swept.
2. Bead context: store.list_all() in evaluate() reads the home workspace beads, not the workspace being analyzed. The agent's dedup context is wrong for non-default workspaces.

Fix: extend WeaveStrand to accept Vec<PathBuf> of workspaces (default + explore). In evaluate(), iterate workspaces, find the one with the most-elapsed cooldown that has doc files, create a workspace-local bead store via BrCliBeadStore::discover(workspace), and run the gap analysis with that workspace's docs and beads. State files are already workspace-keyed via SHA-256 hash, so per-workspace cooldowns work without changes.

Changes needed:
- src/strand/weave.rs: change workspace: PathBuf to workspaces: Vec<PathBuf>; add store factory (or call BrCliBeadStore::discover inline); evaluate() iterates workspaces picking the first with elapsed cooldown + docs
- src/strand/mod.rs:from_config: pass [config.workspace.default] + config.strands.explore.workspaces to WeaveStrand
- Update WeaveConfig or StrandRunner so the workspace list is available at construction time
- Update tests to cover multi-workspace iteration, correct bead store per workspace, and cooldown-based workspace selection

title: fix(explore): parse_beads must handle JSONL output from br ready
description: parse_beads used serde_json::from_str::<Vec<Bead>> expecting a JSON array. br ready --json emits JSONL (one object per line). Every workspace query silently failed with a parse error, causing explore to skip all workspaces. Fix: try JSON array first, fall back to JSONL line-by-line in src/bead_store/mod.rs.

title: Phase 4: Retrospective instructions in pluck template — structured learning block
description: Extend the pluck prompt template with retrospective instructions. Before closing a bead, the agent writes a structured ## Retrospective block: What worked, What didnt, Surprise, Reusable pattern. Block is included in br close --body content. Consolidator later extracts these blocks for learnings.md. Success: >80% of closed beads contain a retrospective block. Plan ref: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 4 Bead Retrospectives section.

title: Trace sanitization with gitleaks rules
description: Traces sanitized before write using vendored gitleaks rules (222 patterns). Aho-Corasick keyword pre-filter skips irrelevant rules; sanitization adds <10ms per trace file. Custom patterns in .needle.yaml applied alongside gitleaks rules. needle update-rules fetches latest gitleaks.toml from upstream. Plan Phase 4: Self-Learning.

title: P1: Core types and enums module
description:
## Task
Define all core types and enums that the rest of the codebase depends on.
These types enforce exhaustive matching — the compiler guarantees every
variant is handled. This is the primary defense against the undefined-path
bugs that caused v1 failures.

## Background
v1 had no type system. Exit codes were checked with ad-hoc if/else chains,
outcomes were implicit, and missing handlers were invisible until runtime.
The types module makes every possible state and outcome explicit and
compiler-enforced. If a new variant is added, every match site must be
updated or the build fails.

## Deliverables

### State enum
BOOTING, SELECTING, CLAIMING, RETRYING, BUILDING, DISPATCHING, EXECUTING,
HANDLING, LOGGING, EXHAUSTED, STOPPED, ERRORED

### Outcome enum
Success, Failure, Timeout, Crash(i32), AgentNotFound, Interrupted

### StrandResult enum
BeadFound(Vec<Bead>), WorkCreated, NoWork, Error(StrandError)

### ClaimResult enum
Claimed(Bead), RaceLost { claimed_by: String }, NotClaimable { reason: String }

### ClaimOutcome enum
Claimed(Bead), AllRaceLost, NoCandidates, StoreError(Error)

### Bead struct
id, title, body, priority, status, assignee, labels, workspace, dependencies,
created_at, updated_at

### BeadId newtype
Wraps String with Display, FromStr, Hash, Eq impls.

### Error types
NeedleError enum with variants for each Tier (Transient, BeadScoped, WorkerScoped).
Implement std::error::Error. Include context (which bead, which workspace, etc.).

### InputMethod enum
Stdin, File { path_template: String }, Args { flag: String }

### PeerStatus enum
Alive { last_seen, current_bead }, Stale { last_seen, claimed_bead }, Dead { heartbeat_file }

## Acceptance Criteria
- All enums derive Debug, Clone, PartialEq at minimum
- All enums have #[non_exhaustive] where future variants are expected
- Bead struct implements serde::Deserialize for JSON parsing from br output
- BeadId implements all comparison/hash traits
- NeedleError has Display impl with human-readable messages
- Unit tests verify serialization/deserialization roundtrips
- No wildcard (_) matches anywhere — all arms are explicit

## Considerations
- These types are the contract between all modules. Changes here ripple
  everywhere, so get them right. Prefer adding optional fields (Option<T>)
  over breaking changes.
- The Outcome enum must NOT have a catch-all. The classify() function maps
  every exit code range to a specific variant. Unknown codes map to Failure
  explicitly (not via _).
close_reason: Implemented all core types: BeadId newtype, Bead struct, WorkerState/Outcome/StrandResult/ClaimResult/ClaimOutcome/InputMethod/PeerStatus enums, ProcessOutput struct, NeedleError with ErrorTier, WorkerId type alias. 9 serde roundtrip and classify unit tests pass. Updated all modules to use new types. cargo build/test/clippy all clean.
